claims.statement: The implemented scalar, O(2) matter and metric field equations (diagonal and t-x off-diagonal components) of the UET parent code follow from the Theory Card action UET-PARENT-ACTION-001.
claims.note: Mathematical consistency only; says nothing about whether nature follows this action.

claims.statement: epsilon is not an independent coupling of the parent action: in canonical variables xi_c and m_psi are epsilon-independent, lambda_psi ~ 1/epsilon and g_c ~ sqrt(epsilon), so epsilon = 0 is a degenerate point rather than a continuous GR limit.

Assuming ordinary matter couples minimally to the Jordan metric, the UET parent action maps onto the Damour-Esposito-Farese class with alpha0 = 0 and beta0 = -2 xi_c around psi0 = 0, so PPN gamma - 1 = 0 at that background.
claims.note: Mathematical mapping only; confrontation with binary-pulsar data is W6 (Test Card T001).

claims.note: CONSTRAINT (not a prediction): xi_c in [2.0, 2.4] excluded for m_psi <= 2.5e-18 eV; L2 promotion approved by the author 2026-11-09.

claims.statement: In the layer-3 model, systems that disappear when their free-energy store F is exhausted at burn power P give steady abundance N* = b F/P (Little's law), replicator dynamics with fitness aR - P/F as an identity, and selection of the lowest R* = P/(a F) under a shared resource, without imposed payoffs.
claims.note: Mathematical consistency of the author's persistence-selection logic; no empirical confrontation yet.

claims.statement: The layer-3 abundance law N = b F/P, with stellar-model lifetimes and independently measured helium, predicts the horizontal-to-red-giant-branch star ratio in old globular clusters to within about 5 percent (R_pred = 1.467 +/- 0.023 vs R_obs = 1.39 +/- 0.03), a 2.05 sigma tension.
claims.note: CONSTRAINT, outcome INCONCLUSIVE by the preregistered rule (2 < z <= 3). Not a falsification and not a pass. L2 recording approved by the author 2026-11-09.

claims.statement: In the parent action, matter (the O(2) field) exchanges energy-momentum only with the response field, at the derived rate d^mu T_mu_nu = (1/2) eps h |chi|^2 d_nu phi on the matter shell; with h = 0 matter is separately conserved.
claims.note: Supports author point 2 mathematically. Calling the response field 'structure of space' is an interpretation.

claims.statement: The parent action's symmetries give the conserved quantities Noether's theorems require for the implemented equations: the O(2) charge (chi number) is conserved with the portal on; diffeomorphism invariance gives the generalized Bianchi identity nabla^mu E_mu_nu = -kappa (E_phi d_nu phi + sum_A E_A d_nu chi_A) for the implemented residuals, so the total energy-momentum of matter, response field and geometry is conserved while matter energy alone is not; in flat space energy, momentum, angular momentum and the boost charge are conserved, the boost charge only because phi and chi share one light cone.
claims.note: Covers O(2), diffeomorphisms (Bianchi I; an inhomogeneous metric in t, x with g_tx, and a full metric with all ten components depending on t, x, y, z), translations and boosts (1+1 lattice) and rotations (2+1 lattice). Nearest known theory: Noether 1918, ADM constraint, Poincare charges. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: The canonical UET potential has a true vacuum with psi0 != 0 when chi condenses (m2_chi < 0), and can have one with all masses positive when lam_chi is small (explicit example); then alpha0 != 0 and gamma_PPN != 1. A sufficient condition for psi0 = 0 is m2_chi > 0 and g_c^2 <= 2 lam_chi m2_psi.
claims.note: A falsification route for a future Test Card (Cassini); not yet confronted with data. With chi = ordinary matter (author 2026-11-10) the condensate branch m2_chi < 0 is excluded; only the metastable branch remains.

claims.statement: With chi identified as ordinary matter, the UET portal produces a composition-independent Yukawa force V = -G M m/r [1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)] with alpha = g_c^2/(2 kappa m_chi^4) and lambda = 1/m_psi.
claims.note: Derived relation; not yet confronted with inverse-square-law, lunar or planetary data (planned Test Card T005).

claims.statement: With chi as ordinary matter, published fifth-force bounds limit the UET portal coupling: g_c < 5.1e-10 eV for m_psi <= 5.1e-3 eV (torsion balance) and g_c < 3.9e-15 eV at m_psi = 1.0e-15 eV (lunar laser ranging).
claims.note: CONSTRAINT, not a prediction; g_c remains free. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: For a mode that is part of a closed Hamiltonian system with an ohmic environment, the open-system layer-2 laws emerge without being assumed: friction, burn power P = gamma x'^2, noise obeying the KMS/equipartition relation, heat flow from hot to cold, and exponential free-energy decay (P proportional to F).
claims.note: Supports author points 1, 4 and 8 at model level. Standard open-system physics (Caldeira-Leggett 1983); not yet tied to the parent-action fields.

claims.statement: With lifetimes derived from the layer-2 burn law, tau = integral dF/P(F), selection still favours the lowest R* = 1/(a tau), but tau = F0/P0 holds only for regulated burners; with two resources a mixed equilibrium exists and is Nash-stable against rare invaders.
claims.note: Supports author points 4 and 10 at model level. Ecology analogue: Tilman resource-ratio theory; not new physics by itself.

claims.statement: Each UET layer reduces to an established theory (layer 1: DEF scalar-tensor with a Yukawa portal; layer 2: Caldeira-Leggett open systems; layer 3: exactly the Tilman chemostat consumer-resource model). The only cross-layer effect found, a preferred-frame portal drag F = Gamma v q^2/(12 pi R), depends on three free parameters, so UET currently makes no numerical prediction that differs from standard physics.
claims.note: A negative result: the Theory Card's 'differences' field stays 'none yet', now with evidence.

claims.statement: The Sun's energy use (luminosity plus solar wind) is written into its gravitational parameter at the rate general relativity gives: predicted -8.76e-14 +/- 1.0e-14 per year against the MESSENGER measurement -6.13e-14 +/- 1.47e-14 (z = 1.48); no gravitational trace at all is disfavoured at 4.2 sigma.
claims.note: Supports author point 7 through standard physics; does not distinguish UET from GR. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: Multimode laser rate equations are the layer-3 selection model term for term (a = stimulated-emission coefficient, tau = photon lifetime, F = 1, R = inversion); R* is the threshold inversion, one shared inversion gives single-mode lasing with gain clamping, and two inversion pools give two-mode coexistence.
claims.note: Shows author point 5 (selection by resource use, without learning) in a non-living physical system. Standard laser physics.

claims.statement: The trace that energy use leaves in the environment is the entropy production Sigma, which splits exactly into a readable record I(S:R) and a potential difference D (free energy T*D left in the environment); at long times D dominates, and the number of bits written is Sigma/ln 2, not Q/(kT ln 2).
claims.note: Author clarification 2026-11-10: the trace is a number or potential difference, not a new thing in the universe. Standard non-equilibrium physics.

claims.statement: Layer-3 resource selection with two essential resources predicts, from monoculture physiology alone, the dominance and coexistence regions of Tilman's (1977) diatom chemostats: predicted Si/P boundaries 86.9 and 6.2 against observed about 80 and 6; 2 of 3 ratio groups match fully and the Si/P = 38 group partly.
claims.note: Path-A test outside physics. Re-analysis with the same model Tilman used, not an independent experiment. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: The burn-law lifetime of a passive burner (P ~ F^(7/2), Mestel cooling) plus the abundance law reproduces the slope of the SDSS white dwarf luminosity function: predicted 2/7 = 0.286 against observed 0.320 per magnitude (|log10| = 0.049).
claims.note: Path-A test in astronomy. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: The abundance law N = b tau holds for the 238U-234U decay chain: the half-life inferred from secular-equilibrium abundances (245,670 +/- 260 yr) matches one measured without equilibrium (244,900 +/- 1340 yr), z = 0.56.
claims.note: Path-A test in nuclear physics. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-10.

claims.statement: A source observed through a finite-speed signal is recorded at its retarded time, and the error of treating the record as the present equals the rate of change times the record age at first order.
claims.note: Principle P2 of the thought experiment v3. Standard physics; model-level check.

claims.statement: Two systems share a record (mutual information) only after causal contact by overlapping past cones, t >= d/(2c), earlier than the direct signal d/c; before contact the shared record is super-exponentially small.
claims.note: Principle P4 of the thought experiment v3, corrected by this test (common past). Classical Gaussian toy model.

claims.statement: An observer that keeps a history of records estimates the present with a bias one order lower than one that treats the newest record as the present, but amplifies measurement noise, so memory helps only below a crossover noise level.
claims.note: Research item 5 of the thought experiment: Markov versus history-dependent model, in a linear-Gaussian toy.

claims.statement: The canonical response scalar of the parent action propagates only inside the light cone: the PDE solution converges at second order to the exact retarded solution and the field vanishes outside the cone.
claims.note: Links the observation layer to the core equation at linear order, flat background, 1+1D only; the full nonlinear curved-space statement is open.

claims.statement: Seeing a distant event and being present with it are separated by two different delays: the record age at arrival exceeds 2d/c for every timelike journey started when the record arrives, whatever is spent, while the traveller's own ageing can be made arbitrarily short only by converting rest mass, at photon-rocket mass ratio m0/m1 >= exp(2 eta) = (gamma (1 + beta))^2 for start and stop.
claims.note: Extends principle P2: at arrival the gap is Xdot times an age above 2d/c. Both bounding events lie on the source worldline, so 2d/c does not depend on the one-way synchronisation convention. Textbook special relativity, flat spacetime; not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: Records of one event carried by gravitational waves and by light travel at the same speed: c_T = 1 of the parent action lies inside the GW170817 bound (v_GW - v_EM)/v_EM in [-3e-15, +7e-16].
claims.note: First real-data test of the observation layer (principle P1) together with layer 1. Not UET-distinct: any c_T = 1 theory passes. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-11.

claims.statement: Principle P2 holds for pulsating stars in binaries: the pulsation-timing delay amplitude equals the light-travel record age predicted from an independent RV orbit (PM/RV = 1.006, z = 0.04 for KIC 6780873; 1.021, z = 0.17 for KIC 5705575).
claims.note: First non-circular real-data test of P2 (about 10% precision). Not UET-distinct: standard light-travel time passes. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-11.

claims.statement: Principle P4 as corrected by O2 holds in a quenched quantum many-body chain: the correlation front stays below the common-past bound c_a + c_b (excess -0.36 and -4.35 sigma at U/J = 7 and 9) and exceeds the direct-contact-only bound by 3.9 and 6.0 sigma, so contact through a common past is required.
claims.note: First real-data test of P4. The one-sided bound is weak by itself; the direct-contact diagnostic carries the content. Not UET-distinct: standard quasiparticle picture passes. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-11.

claims.statement: Principle P3 holds as part of the Lorentz time transformation: the Ives-Stilwell observable of 7Li+ ions at beta = 0.338 is (1.47 +- 2.30)e-9, consistent with the zero the boost of the parent action's local frame requires (z = 0.64); absolute time is excluded.
claims.note: Tests P3 only as part of the Lorentz time transformation, not relative simultaneity in isolation. Not UET-distinct: special relativity passes. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-11.

claims.statement: The portal drag, the only cross-layer UET effect found, must satisfy Gamma g_c^2 <= 9.1e-44 eV^3 for the planets to have survived 4.5672 Gyr in the Sun's rest frame; at the T005 bound on g_c the friction time of the response scalar exceeds about 60 years.
claims.note: A derived bound, not a prediction. Assumes the Sun's rest frame as the environment frame; a different environment frame (for example the CMB frame) needs its own analysis.

claims.statement: Under the parent action with chi = ordinary matter, the response-scalar friction is not a free parameter: it is the linear-response dissipation of the ambient matter, zero in vacuum, and the resulting portal drag equals alpha^2 times gravitational dynamical friction, so it is not a UET-distinct effect.
claims.note: Supersedes the free-Gamma assumption of B4 and B5 (those records stay unchanged). Classical ideal-gas medium, linear response, non-relativistic matter. A different bath for psi would need new fields in the action.

claims.statement: In the closed matter-plus-environment model of layer 2, the subsystem's free energy relative to the environment obeys dF/dt = -P with P = T sigma >= 0 (Markov limit), so the layer-3 lifetime tau = integral dF/P follows from the dynamics; tau = F/P is the special case of constant P.
claims.note: Linear Caldeira-Leggett mode with an ohmic classical bath; not yet derived for the psi field of the parent action itself. Standard stochastic thermodynamics, not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: With ordinary matter as the only bath of the response scalar, free psi waves are not absorbed at linear order (Cherenkov condition), and the free energy that psi burns is that of sourced fields moving relative to matter, at the rate P = F_drag v given by linear response, which exact classical orbits confirm.
claims.note: Classical, collisionless, non-relativistic medium; collisional absorption is second order and not included. Standard kinetic theory, not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: The parent action needs no free energy reference to give SI numbers: its parameters carry mass dimension, so with chi identified as a particle the conversion uses only hbar and c. Its chi sector is the relativistic O(2) Bose fluid whose non-relativistic limit is Gross-Pitaevskii with lam = 8 pi a m, and the psi portal adds a scattering-length shift delta_a = -alpha G M^3 / m_psi^2, which at the T005 bound is 5e-18 of the Rb-87 value.
claims.note: Tree level, uniform fluid, chi = nucleon lane as in T005. Liquid He II is outside the tree-level GP class (n a^3 >= 0.38), so the legacy Topic 13 identification of Phi with the superfluid fraction is not obtained from the action. Standard physics, not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: Lane hypothesis assumed by Topic 13: with chi as the He-4 atom, superfluid He II is the condensed phase of the parent action's O(2) sector, so at tree level with lam = 8 pi a m from the measured He-He scattering length its first sound equals the Bogoliubov speed.
claims.note: FAILED in T015 (2026-11-16): tree-level sound speed 848 m/s against 233.1 m/s, D = 2.31. A failure removes only this lane (chi = atom, tree level), not the parent action; the chi = nucleon lane of T005 is unaffected.

claims.statement: If the portal source is the nucleon rest-energy density (chi = nucleon) while gravity couples to total mass-energy, the portal force is composition dependent at the level of the nucleon-number-to-mass ratio: for a uniform source sphere, eta = alpha eps_S (eps_1 - eps_2) F(R/lambda) e^{-r/lambda}(1 + r/lambda), and eta = 0 when the portal source is total mass.
claims.note: AI interpretation: the action has no nuclear forces, so whether binding energy sources the portal is a lane choice, not derived. Standard composition-dependent fifth-force physics, not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: With the nucleon-number portal lane, MICROSCOPE's eta(Ti, Pt) limits the portal to alpha < 5.1e-12 and g_c < 1.16e-15 eV for lambda >= 1e8 m (m_psi <= 2e-15 eV), 11.6 times tighter in alpha than lunar laser ranging (T005).
claims.note: Constraint, not a prediction. Valid only if binding energy does not source the portal (AI lane choice, C_PORTAL_COMPOSITION_EP). L2 approved by the author 2026-11-17.

claims.statement: With a formation rate growing as e^{lambda t}, the layer-3 abundance of a phase entered at age a1 and lasting tau is N = b_now (e^{-lambda a1} - e^{-lambda (a1+tau)})/lambda, which reduces to N = b tau as lambda -> 0; for asynchronously dividing cells with cycle T the phase fraction is 2 (2^{-a1/T} - 2^{-a2/T}), confirmed by an agent model with 10 percent cycle-time spread to 0.005.
claims.note: Standard age-distribution result of cell kinetics; extends the engine to growing populations (topic 0.22 lane card). A fixed cycle never relaxes to the stable distribution; variability is needed for mixing. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: For unequal division with parent cycle P and daughter cycle D sharing a budded period B, the layer-3 law with a growing formation rate gives the doubling time from 2^{-P/T} + 2^{-D/T} = 1, the unbudded-daughter fraction (1 - e^{-a U_d}) / [(1 - e^{-a U_d}) + (1 - e^{-a U_p})] with a = ln 2 / T, and the budded fraction 2^{B/T} - 1; an agent model with 10 percent spread agrees, and P = D recovers equal division.
claims.note: Reproduces the age-distribution analysis of Hartwell and Unger (1977); standard cell kinetics, not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: The layer-3 abundance law for unequal division connects single-cell yeast cycle times to population growth: the doubling time computed from parent and daughter generation times agrees with the counted doubling time in all five Hartwell-Unger conditions (max z = 1.81).
claims.note: Constraint, not a prediction; not blind; not UET-distinct. L2 approved by the author 2026-11-17.

claims.statement: Layer-3 scope declared by the author (2026-11-17): the lifespan of an animal is its lifetime reserve divided by its metabolic rate, with the same reserve per gram in every species, so the lifetime energy potential (metabolic rate per gram times maximum longevity) is independent of body mass and the same in birds and mammals.
claims.note: FAILED in T018 (2026-11-17): birds have 2.47 times the lifetime energy per gram of mammals (d = 0.392, 95 percent interval 0.330 to 0.455, fail threshold 0.30) and LEP falls with mass (s = -0.114). Removes only this lifespan scope of layer 3; tau = F/P for closed reserves and N = b tau are unaffected. UET-distinct: the null (current biology) does not fail. Design: topics/0.23_Unity_Scale_Link/Doc/STRESS_02_LAYER3_SCOPE.md.

claims.statement: With the nucleon-number portal lane, the Eot-Wash Rot-Wash equivalence-principle data limit the portal to alpha <= 6.4e-6 and g_c <= 1.30e-12 eV for 2 m <= lambda <= 1e5 m, weakening to alpha <= 0.50 at 1 cm.
claims.note: Constraint, not a prediction; g_c = 0 admissible. Not UET-distinct. Valid only if binding energy does not source the portal (AI lane choice, C_PORTAL_COMPOSITION_EP). L2 approved by the author 2026-11-17.

claims.statement: AI proposal for route B: if the rate of free-energy destruction sources psi with a reciprocal coupling (charge Q = a M + beta P), lunar laser ranging limits the shared time constant tau_beta = beta/sqrt(4 pi G) to at most 4.61e15 s (1.46e8 yr) for psi ranges much longer than 1 AU.
claims.note: Constraint, not a prediction; tau_beta = 0 admissible. The coupling is not in the approved Theory Card. tau_beta = 1/H0 would exceed the LLR limit about 9,900 times. L2 approved by the author 2026-11-17.

claims.statement: AI translation of the author's statement (2026-11-17) that innovation saves resources, time included: in the historical succession of lighting technologies no successor that replaced an incumbent used more energy per lumen-hour and more hours of work per lumen-hour than the incumbent at the time it entered.
claims.note: Stage 1 of test D (topics/0.25_Strategy_Power_Economics/Doc/ANALYSIS_EXTERNAL_ENERGY_UET_2026-11-17.md section 6). Needs no exchange rate between time and energy. Not UET-distinct: standard economics expects the same. Run 2026-11-17: PASS, 2 DOMINATES, 5 TRADE_OFF, 0 WORSE_BOTH at the device energy basis. L2 approved by the author 2026-11-18; device energy basis only.

claims.statement: The two-way speed of light depends neither on orientation nor on laboratory velocity, as the Lorentz boost of the parent action's local frame requires: Michelson-Morley P_MM = (4 +- 8)e-12 (z = 0.50, Herrmann et al. 2009) and Kennedy-Thorndike P_KT = (-4.8 +- 3.7)e-8 (z = 1.30, Tobar et al. 2010); contraction without time dilation is excluded.
claims.note: With T013 all three Robertson-Mansouri-Sexl parameters are tested. Not UET-distinct: special relativity passes. First run failed on a 64-bit rounding defect; amendment 1 approved before the rerun. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-18.

claims.statement: In the fast, weak-draw limit of the shared pool, UET layer 3 reduces term by term to the Lotka-Volterra competition model of Saavedra et al. (2025): r_i = a_i S/delta - 1/tau_i, a_ij = (a_j F_j)/(a_i F_i), K_i = r_i delta^2/(a_i^2 F_i S); with F ~ M, P ~ M^(3/4), a ~ M^(-1/4) the biomass interaction matrix is their Eq. (14).
claims.note: Nearest known theory: MacArthur consumer-resource reduction and metabolic coexistence theory. UET adds mortality from the burn law (1/tau = P/F); one pool gives one winner, so coexistence needs more than one resource.

claims.statement: A species-level lifetime reserve set by extrinsic mortality (author, 2026-11-18) is partly supported: bats spend 1.96 times the lifetime energy per gram of other mammals (d_bat = 0.29, CI 0.19-0.40) but less than birds (d_bat - d_bird = -0.17, CI -0.28 to -0.07); flight accounts for about 60 percent of the bird offset. INCONCLUSIVE under T023. With a phylogenetic correction (T025, PGLS on a TimeTree tree) the central values stay close (d_bat = 0.235, Delta = -0.198) but the intervals widen about tenfold (d_bat -0.31 to 0.78), so the data cannot decide: INCONCLUSIVE under T025.
claims.note: Not blind; bat torpor biases the bat value upward; T023 has no phylogenetic correction; T025 adds it (tree kept local, TimeTree forbids redistribution). Nearest theory: disposable soma and extrinsic-mortality theory of ageing; not UET-distinct. L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-18.

claims.statement: With the O(2) matter field chi as a free thermal bath, the parent action gives the response field phi a one-loop Schwinger-Keldysh self-energy whose Wightman functions obey KMS (Pi> = exp(w/T) Pi<); the damping rate is rho/(2w), the pair-decay width at T = 0 is the textbook one, and long-wavelength modes get ohmic friction gamma(q,T) = N sigma^2 n(sqrt(q^2/4 + M_chi^2))/(16 pi q) with sigma = h sqrt(eps)/(Z sqrt(k)).
claims.note: Derives the layer 2 friction that uet_layer2_dissipation.py assumed. Nearest known theory: Feynman-Vernon and Caldeira-Leggett with a field-theory bath; warm-inflation dissipation. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: With the action-derived spectral function of phi (C_L2_FROM_ACTION), rho(w,q) > 0 for w > 0, heat between a phi mode at T_phi and the chi bath at T flows from hot to cold, the entropy production J (1/T - 1/T_phi) is nonnegative and zero only at equilibrium, and a coherent mode burns free energy at P = Gamma E, writing P/T of entropy and P/(T ln 2) bits per unit time.
claims.note: Layer 2 second law and burn chain for the portal channel follow from the action. Nearest known theory: Kubo linear response, detailed balance, Landauer. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: With the one-loop spectral function of the parent action, a phi mode in a chi medium grows at a_i R - 1/tau_i, where the death rate 1/tau_i is the layer 2 damping rate rho_sink/(2w) and the capture a_i = -rho_stream/(2w) is exact and linear in the stream strength R; isotropic pools of any distribution only damp phi, a chi stream moving at v feeds exactly the modes with w < v q, and with these rates layer 3 selection keeps only the lowest R* = 1/(a_i tau_i).
claims.note: Layer 3 capture and death rates follow from the action for the portal channel; supply, loss and the set of modes do not. Nearest known theory: laser rate equations and mode competition, beam-plasma Cherenkov instability, consumer-resource ecology. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: With the parent action's chi self-coupling lam = lambda/Z^2, the layer 3 stream pool loses particles at delta = n_sink <sigma_tot v> with sigma_tot = 3 lam^2/(2 pi s); the supply S is not fixed by the action (S = 0 in a region holding only its fields), and a phi mode persists in steady state only if the boundary supply exceeds S* = delta R*_min.
claims.note: The pool loss follows from the action; the supply is a boundary flux set by an enclosing system. Nearest known theory: beam attenuation, chemostat dilution, laser pump threshold. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: The environment that receives a system's entropy (the divider, at T_c) sets both its resource and its ability to persist: the usable part of a heat store is the exergy C[(T0 - T_c) - T_c ln(T0/T_c)], which vanishes as C (T0 - T_c)^2/(2 T0) when the divider is as warm as the store (alone), and a structure that needs work W_m through linear contacts persists only if T_c <= T_c* = (sqrt(T_h) - sqrt(W_m/K))^2 with K = K_h K_c/(K_h + K_c), a sink threshold beside the supply threshold S* of C_L3_SUPPLY.
claims.note: Exergy and endoreversible (Novikov) thermodynamics; not UET-distinct. Adds the divider temperature to the layer-3 resource and persistence language. Linear heat transfer, fixed divider temperature, no chains. Holds for stores with positive heat capacity only; systems held together by gravity behave oppositely (C_L3_GRAVITATING_DIVIDER).

claims.statement: When the waste heat of one structure is the environment of the next, a chain of N structures between a source at T0 and a final divider at T_N creates no resource: its largest total work rate is K_chain (sqrt(T0) - sqrt(T_N))^2 with every contact in series, so each extra hand-off lowers it (to 1/N for equal contacts); at a given entropy flux the shares between stages are zero-sum, and the chain persists only if the sum of the stages' needs is below that maximum.
claims.note: Extends C_L3_ENTROPY_DIVIDER to chains. Endoreversible series engines with linear contacts; not UET-distinct. Radiative contacts and warming dividers are open.

claims.statement: In a chain of entropy dividers whose contacts follow J = G (T_h^n - T_c^n)/n, sharing between stages is zero-sum only for linear contacts (n = 1): for radiation (n = 4) and any n > 1 a unit of work taken by an upstream stage costs the downstream stages more than one unit (marginal cost c > 1), so the way the upstream stage uses its share changes what the whole chain gets; for n < 1 the opposite holds (c < 1).
claims.note: Extends C_L3_ENTROPY_CHAIN. The effect is small unless a contact works near its limit (c = 1.015 in the illustrative sun-planet-space case). Endoreversible engines with radiative contacts; not UET-distinct. Sunlight dilution and warming dividers are open.

claims.statement: A system held together by gravity has negative heat capacity (C = -(3/2) N k in virial equilibrium), so against a colder divider it does not run down but heats and moves away from the divider, exponentially at rate G/|C| for a linear contact and diverging in finite time 4|C|/(3 G T0^3) for radiation into 0 K; two bodies with C1 < 0 and C2 > 0 settle only if C2 < |C1| (Lynden-Bell and Wood), so a divider of unlimited capacity such as space never lets a gravitating system settle, while the usable fraction 1 - T_c/T of the energy it loses rises with time.
claims.note: Limits the scope of C_L3_ENTROPY_DIVIDER (positive heat capacity only). Thermodynamics of self-gravitating systems; not UET-distinct. Black holes as dividers and cosmic expansion are open.

claims.statement: A black hole used as the divider gets colder as it receives energy (C = -8 pi G M^2 k/(hbar c) < 0, dS/dE = 1/T_H), so unlike ordinary dividers it improves as matter piles in; it is the largest entropy store (about 1.8e90 k for Sgr A*), every hole above 4.5e22 kg is colder than today's CMB and grows, and its evaporation is a layer-3 burn with P ~ F^-2 whose lifetime is F0/(3 P0), one third of the naive store-over-power estimate.
claims.note: Schwarzschild black-hole thermodynamics and the generalised second law; not UET-distinct. Links the author's black-hole picture to the divider waves and to C_L3_BURN_LAW_SELECTION. Rotation, accretion and cosmic expansion are open.

claims.statement: In flat Lambda-CDM (Planck 2018) the last divider is the cosmic event horizon: it is cold but not at zero (T_dS = hbar H_L/(2 pi k) = 2.2e-30 K, so no process reaches efficiency 1), its capacity is finite (S_dS = 3.3e122 k, a ceiling on all entropy, the traces of author item 9, the universe can hold), and it takes over in sequence: the background becomes colder than a solar-mass black hole at 3.2e11 yr and than Sgr A* at 5.9e11 yr, falls below T_dS at 1.2e12 yr, and every hole lighter than c^3/(4 G H_L) = 5.6e52 kg eventually evaporates into the horizon.
claims.note: Lambda-CDM and de Sitter horizon thermodynamics; not UET-distinct. Closes the divider sequence of waves D1-D5 (store, chain, radiation, gravity, black hole, horizon). Radiation era, w != -1 and the bath interpretation of the horizon are open.

claims.statement: A lone freely falling body in Lambda-only (de Sitter) space is not alone: the horizon is a bath at T_dS = hbar H/(2 pi k) that receives C (T0 - T)/T_dS of entropy while the body loses only C ln(T0/T), and the body approaches T_dS only as a limit (rate 4 sigma A T_dS^3/C), never 0 K; but the bath's thermal wavelength is exactly 4 pi^2 c/H, larger than the horizon, so no body inside couples to it as a blackbody and the relaxation time (at least 1e94 yr for a 1 m rock) is a lower bound.
claims.note: Stefan cooling plus Gibbons-Hawking; not UET-distinct. Model A of the author's two-space picture (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4, 2026-11-22): space of the first kind divides entropy in principle but infinitely slowly; in practice other matter and radiation divide it (model B). Sharpens SYNTHESIS_AUDIT C2. Correction 2026-11-23: uses the measured Lambda and its horizon bath, which acts as a divider, so it is not the author's one-object universe (see D11).

claims.statement: When bodies fall together, frying (dynamical friction) sinks a mass M from r_i in t = 1.17 r_i^2 v_c/(G M lnL) and hands the light sea entropy 2 (M/m) ln(r_i/r_f), so the sea is the divider of the heavy body; mixing (a non-spinning black-hole merger) radiates at least 5.72 % of mu c^2 and at most 1 - sqrt(m1^2 + m2^2)/(m1 + m2) of the mass, and multiplies the entropy by 2 (1 - eps)^2 for equal masses, so mixing out-produces frying by about 82 orders of magnitude in the illustrative case.
claims.note: Chandrasekhar dynamical friction, Schwarzschild circular orbits and the Hawking area theorem; not UET-distinct. Model B of the author's two-space picture (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4, 2026-11-22). Mass is lost on mixing, measurable from outside in GR. The radiated wave is coherent and carries little entropy (AI inference). T029 (2026-11-23, numbered T028 when run): 225 of 227 nearly non-spinning GWTC mergers radiate between 0.0572 eta and the area cap; median 3.13 times the inspiral loss; weak test, GR-derived final masses; the frying branch is not tested. L2 approved by the author. Correction 2026-11-23: the author's stir-fry analogy was an illustration (in SR being pushed and collapsing together look alike), not a model; D8 and T029 are AI readings of it, not the author's hypothesis (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4).

claims.statement: When one black hole evaporates completely in Lambda-only space, space returns to what it was: isotropic emission leaves exactly zero gravitational-wave memory and behind the outgoing radiation the metric is pure de Sitter; the record of the mass is the radiation, which passes the hole's horizon after ln2/H = 12.1 Gyr and redshifts, and the permanent lag (G/(r c^2)) int M dt of clocks that were near it; the lifetime is M_eq^3 (atanh x0 - atan x0)/(2a), which reduces to F0/(3 P0) for small holes.
claims.note: Hawking evaporation, Birkhoff with Lambda and gravitational-wave memory; not UET-distinct. Supports the author's 2026-11-22 split between space and record (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4): the record needs radiation or matter, not space. The two horizon temperatures belong to different observers; the flux balance mixes frames (stated). Correction 2026-11-23: uses the measured Lambda, and the Hawking radiation is itself a second thing, so it is not the author's one-object universe (see D11).

claims.statement: In the real universe the record of a vanished mass splits three ways: radiation emitted today escapes intergalactic matter (Thomson optical depth over the whole future 7.3e-4, so at least 99.9 % is never scattered); records from the dense early universe were absorbed by matter (optical depth 2.4 by z = 100 if ionised, opaque before recombination); and asymmetric events leave a permanent geometric memory, for a circular-binary merger Delta h = G E sin^2 i (17 + cos^2 i)/(24 c^4 r), while space described by Lambda alone keeps nothing in either model.
claims.note: Thomson optical depth and nonlinear gravitational-wave memory; not UET-distinct. Real-universe counterpart of C_L3_EVAPORATION_RECORD. In the author's 2026-11-22 split (AI interpretation): the first kind of space keeps nothing; the geometry made by mass-energy keeps asymmetric events; matter keeps early records as heat.

claims.statement: In GR without Lambda, one body alone in free fall radiates and dissipates exactly nothing (conserved mass and momentum, quadrupole quadratic in time; a spherical pulsation also emits nothing), so a lone free fall uses no energy; any loss needs something else: the body's own non-spherical internal motion (32 G (I1 - I2)^2 omega^6 / (5 c^5) for a spinning body), a second body (P = (32/5) G^4 M^2 m^2 (M + m)/(c^5 d^5), falling as m^2; Sun with Earth 196 W) or Lambda's horizon.
claims.note: Birkhoff's theorem, equivalence principle and the quadrupole formula; not UET-distinct. Addresses a lone body in a static, already-existing empty space, without the measured Lambda or horizon bath of D7 and D9. AI interpretation: the author's step from space to behaviour to burning has no GR equation for a single body; a UET law for it would differ from GR here. Limit (author, 2026-11-23): Schwarzschild is static; it puts the body in an empty space that already exists forever, so D11 answers a frozen picture, not the author's universe that begins and is dynamic; that needs a dynamic GR solution (AI candidates: a closed dust Friedmann universe, the Oppenheimer-Snyder interior, Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi).

claims.statement: Space's capacity to take disorder (the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of the final de Sitter horizon, 3.3e122 k) is almost unused today: inside today's event horizon (16.7 Gly) radiation holds 1.4e-34 of it and supermassive black holes about 8e-21 (illustrative inputs); even all matter inside the horizon collapsed into one hole would hold only (Om/OL)^2 (R_eh H_L/c)^6 = 0.157, so matter alone can never fill space.
claims.note: Gibbons-Hawking entropy and the generalised second law; not UET-distinct. Answers the author's 'space is not 100 % open in the dynamic view' (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4, 2026-11-23) with a number. Black-hole inputs are illustrative AI values from memory; a data comparison would need the measured black-hole mass function. AI interpretation: space is open to all but about one part in 10^20 today.

claims.statement: For a system between a hot side T_h and a cold side T_c with heat contacts g_h, g_c, openness K = g_h g_c/(g_h + g_c) sets the ceiling on the work it can draw, P_max = K (sqrt T_h - sqrt T_c)^2 at efficiency 1 - sqrt(T_c/T_h), so more openness allows more kept order; the same openness without the system's own engine gives zero work and the most entropy; a structure that decays at entropy rate sigma_d persists only if K >= T_c sigma_d/(sqrt T_h - sqrt T_c)^2, so a closed system (K -> 0) keeps no order.
claims.note: Endoreversible thermodynamics (Novikov 1957; Curzon and Ahlborn 1975) and the maximum power principle; not UET-distinct. Puts the author's 2026-11-23 statement in one equation (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4): openness is a ceiling, the order needs the system's engine, the environment (T_h, T_c) is a limit, not a choice. The model (Newtonian contacts, reversible core) is an AI choice.

claims.statement: The openness ceiling of D13 composes with the layer-3 pool equation of L3-2: with the drawn work filling the pool, S = eta K (sqrt T_h - sqrt T_c)^2 / e, the steady pool is linear in openness, the two persistence thresholds are one condition (T_c sigma_d = e delta R*_min / eta), a structure survives ln(R_ss/R*_i)/delta after the system closes and appears -ln(1 - R*_i/R_ss)/delta after it opens.
claims.note: Synthesis check, not UET-distinct (chemostat and pump-threshold models, endoreversible thermodynamics). Openness is the enclosing system that L3-2 left open; the author's 'a closed system dies' (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION §4, 2026-11-23) is the survival time after closing, set by the pool leak delta. eta and e are free parameters. FAILED in T030 (2026-11-23): a fasting man's specific mass-loss rate fell (r = 0.922, fail line 0.934), so a closed pool leaking with constant delta does not describe a living reserve after supply stops. The algebra relating thresholds and lifetimes to delta stands as mathematics; a new branch with a varying delta would be a new L0 hypothesis with its own card.

claims.statement: In the full layer-3 model with one structure type (dn/dt = (a R - 1/tau) n, dR/dt = S - delta R - a F R n), the stock M = R + F n loses dM/dt = -(delta R + F n/tau). While supplied, few structures grow by compounding at a S/delta - 1/tau and pull the pool down to R* = 1/(a tau), not to zero. After the supply stops, the specific loss rate starts between delta and 1/tau and ends at min(delta, 1/tau), so the loss slows in the end; it falls monotonically when delta > 1/tau and first rises when delta < 1/tau. A constant rate (D14) needs a one-part store.
claims.note: Answers why T030 failed D14 within layer 3 itself, but was derived after T030 was seen: not tested by it. The author's 'behaviour uses resources to the end' (2026-11-24) appears as structures using the pool down to their threshold R*; the reading is an AI interpretation. Nearest theory: consumer-resource models, two-compartment depletion. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: A freely falling frame removes the uniform part of every outside pull but keeps the tidal part (point mass: eigenvalues (2,-1,-1) G M/d^3; Lambda: +H_L^2 delta_ij). Measured against a bound system's own binding rate G m/r^3, the leftover is about 1e-7 for the Earth (Moon), 5e-12 for the solar system out to Neptune, 0.1 for the Milky Way halo (Andromeda), 0.24 for the Local Group (Lambda; zero-gravity radius 1.6 Mpc) and 6e-3 for the Virgo cluster (Lambda). No frame is free of Lambda; compact bodies are nearly free, groups of galaxies are not.
claims.note: Bounds the one-body universe (D11, C_L3_LONE_BODY_GR): it is a fair model of a piece of ours only where epsilon << 1, and it is a different solution of GR, not a limit of our universe. Whether inertia itself comes from the other matter (Mach's principle) is open and not addressed. Round literature inputs chosen by the AI. Nearest theory: Hill sphere, tidal radius, Lambda zero-gravity radius. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: Inside a slowly rotating spherical shell of mass M and radius R, local inertial frames (what 'not rotating' means for a gyroscope) turn with omega_in/Omega = 4 alpha (2 - alpha)/((1 + alpha)(3 - alpha)), M/R = 2 alpha/(1 + alpha)^2 (G = c = 1): (4/3) G M/(R c^2) in the weak field, rising to full co-rotation as the shell nears its own horizon. Matter inside the Hubble radius has G M/(R c^2) = Omega_m/2 = 0.16 (0.5 for the full critical density), the order-one value at which matter can set the inertial frame.
claims.note: Derived numerically through a shell with tangential stress and checked against Brill and Cohen (1966). The cosmological reading is an AI illustration: a flat-space shell is not an expanding universe, and GR is not Machian in general (Minkowski space has inertia without matter). With D16: a falling frame is free of other bodies neither in its tides nor in its rotation, only nearly so for compact bodies. Nearest theory: Lense-Thirring, Brill-Cohen. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: A spinning body on an orbit is flexed by the tidal field at the rate F = <|dT/dt|^2> seen in its own frame: 18 (GM/a^3)^2 (n - omega)^2 on a circular orbit and 63 (GM/a^3)^2 n^2 e^2 for a locked body on a slightly eccentric orbit. F vanishes only for a circular, synchronous orbit, and at fixed angular momentum that state is the lowest energy the system can reach exactly when mu a^2 > 3 I (Darwin-Hut); otherwise no settled state exists. Dissipating through F, the system reaches the motion that no longer flexes it without being steered.
claims.note: AI reading of the author's 'orbit = motion that does not resist; forced motion is temporary' (AUTHOR_PROPOSITION 4, 2026-11-24): resistance = flexing rate F, settled = F = 0 at the energy minimum. Example chosen by the AI. Testable on measured binaries (circularization cutoff period against age) with a Test Card. Nearest theory: Darwin-Hut-Zahn tidal evolution. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: A flux-limited sample selects by brightness against layer-3 persistence: with luminosity L = eps P, the observed count of a type is N ~ b F eps^(D/2) P^(D/2 - 1), so in three dimensions a type burning 100 times faster is 100 times rarer in space but 10 times more common in the sample, in a thin disk (D = 2) the two selections cancel, and the abundance law n = b F/P can be tested only on volume-limited, 1/V_max-weighted or single-distance samples.
claims.note: Malmquist bias and the 1/V_max estimator; not UET-distinct. Stress test of author item 5: what we see is what persisted and also spent enough energy as light to reach us, so the best resource managers are the hardest to see. T002 unaffected (one distance); T008 unaffected (Hu, Wu and Wu 2007 use 1/(V_max - V_min) weights, checked 2026-11-21).

claims.statement: In steady state with fixed lifetime tau = F/P and light delay r/c, the fraction of a flux-limited sample that still exists when it is observed is A_D = 1 - D lambda/(D + 1) for lambda = d/(c tau) <= 1 and lambda^(-D)/(D + 1) above, with lambda ~ eps^(1/2) P^(3/2)/F; the delay changes which sources are seen but not how many, so a type burning 100 times faster has 1000 times the lambda and in three dimensions a sample of it can be almost entirely sources that are already gone.
claims.note: Light-travel-time and duty-cycle arguments; not UET-distinct. Continues C_OBS_TWO_DELAYS and C_L3_OBSERVED_SELECTION: the light certifies that the source was alive when it left, not now. Euclidean and steady state only.

claims.statement: On the past light cone of flat Lambda-CDM, with a constant comoving birth rate since t = 0 and fixed lifetime tau, the fraction of seen sources that still exist is the ratio of shell integrals of chi^2 a^-1 max(0, min(t_e, tau - t_L)) and chi^2 a^-1 min(tau, t_e); it tends to the static result 1 - 3 lambda/4 for shallow surveys, equals 1 at every depth when tau >= t0, and over the whole cone is 0.107 for tau = 10 Gyr, 44 times the static-space value, because the finite age removes the oldest light.
claims.note: Look-back time and comoving volume; not UET-distinct. Extends C_L3_SEEN_BUT_GONE to expanding space. The constant birth rate is an AI choice.

claims.statement: In a chemostat the layer 3 pool quantities are set by the experimenter: supply S = D S0 (dilution rate times reservoir concentration), loss delta = D and washout 1/tau = D; the persistence threshold S* = delta R*_min holds for any increasing uptake mu(R) with mu(0) = 0, the steady abundance is n* = Y (S0 - R*), and the linear (action-derived) uptake is the special case mu = a R.
claims.note: Derivation and numerical check; S* values for Tilman's diatoms at D = 0.25 per day use the registered T007 physiology and are not a comparison with an outcome. Nearest known theory: chemostat theory (Monod 1950; Novick and Szilard 1950) and Tilman's R* rule. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: When the trace left by resource use changes the environment of later systems (author, 2026-11-19), modelled as a shared trace E written at w per unit resource, fading at kappa and changing capture as a_i0 (1 + beta_i E), layer 3 selection is no longer the supply- and history-independent lowest-R* rule: a trace-helped type takes over above S_c = delta R*_1 + kappa (R*_2(0)/R*_1 - 1)/(w beta_2), the outcome shows hysteresis in the supply between S_b and S_c, and a type that cannot start in an empty environment can replace a pioneer.
claims.note: Derivation and numerical check; the functional form is an AI choice, the channel is the author's. Nearest known theory: niche construction, facilitation in succession, plant-soil feedback and alternative stable states. UET-specific only if w is tied to energy use (bits per joule), which is not yet tested.

claims.statement: Under the trace-feedback model, the shared glucose released by yeast invertase is the trace; with measured invertase kinetics (Koschwanez et al. 2011) the fitted cooperative-growth switch density of yeast in 2 percent sucrose (Dai et al. 2012) corresponds to a shared glucose level G* of about 1.6 mM, an upper estimate, which an independent growth-versus-glucose measurement can confirm or refute.
claims.note: FAILED under T027 (author-approved 2026-11-20): wild-type yeast reaches 0.968 of its maximum exponential rate near 16 mM glucose, ten times above G* = 1.56 mM, so the well-mixed trace reading does not explain the switch. Confronted with Gore et al. (2009) under Test Card T026: INCONCLUSIVE (the designated figure reports a 23 h mean growth rate that never reaches the threshold; exponential rates at two glucose levels lean against 1.6 mM but do not decide). L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-19. Nearest known theory: public-goods models of yeast cooperation (Gore et al. 2009) and Allee effects. Not UET-distinct.

claims.statement: AI hypothesis (stress test 11): selection for persistence raises the readable fraction r of the bits a system writes with its energy; for cells, r = genome bits copied per division / (division energy / (kT ln 2)) rises with effective population size at fixed cell volume.
claims.note: Confronted under Test Card T028: INCONCLUSIVE (only five species in both tables; slope +0.83, 95% CI -0.62 to 2.29). L2 approved by the author on 2026-11-20. Nearest theory: Lynch's drift-barrier hypothesis, which predicts the same sign; not UET-distinct unless the size of the effect is predicted.

claims.statement: Intervals between successive lighting introductions (Nordhaus 1997, Table 1.1) shrink with world population as Delta t ~ N^-(beta-1) with beta = 1.27 (Bettencourt et al. 2007), not as N^-1 (Kremer 1993).
claims.note: T024 FAILED for beta = 1.27 (slope -1.43, 95% -2.14 to -0.72; contains Kremer's -1). For innovation rate against world population the synthesis borrows Kremer (1993), not the urban-scaling exponent. Scope: lighting, world population; urban scaling within cities is not tested. Approved by the author 2026-11-18.
